=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired leaves or whorls visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped near the shoot apex, with short internodes)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade without divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no visible teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (narrow, tapering to a point, widest near the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (sharply pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with lateral veins branching off it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other and perpendicular to the midrib, forming a dense network)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, not elongated, attaching leaf blade to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and brown, typical of young woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: brown (stem is dark brown, consistent with woody tissue)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth with no visible ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipule structures visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky or colored sap visible in any images)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible, and no indication of Fabaceae traits)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils present)

F. Notes: The seedling is marked with a pink tag, likely for identification or monitoring purposes. Some leaves show minor damage, including small holes and slight margin irregularities, but these are not widespread. The surrounding environment includes leaf litter, indicating a forest floor setting, but this is inferred from context and not directly assessed per rules. All images show the same individual seedling from slightly different angles, confirming consistency in morphology.
